# What does this PR do?

Fixes #31981 by adding an informative warning and falling back to DynamicCache if one calls `forward()` directly. Actually DynamicCache will work same as Hybrid, as long as the text sequence stays below sliding window length (i guess 4k). So it should be enough for basic use-cases as in the issue, when a user wants cache for one call only.
pr_comments: The docs for this PR live [here](https://moon-ci-docs.huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_32279). All of your documentation changes will be reflected on that endpoint. The docs are available until 30 days after the last update.

> we have to initialize any cache as long as the person is simply running a forward

So we have to raise error if `use_cache=True` asking to initialize `HybridCache` or set caching to `False`? Can do that, and better with a link to docs. From issue seems like users don't know how to init these new cache classes. 

I made it this way following general trend in transformers, that cache is init by us if user doesn't set it. Is it okay we're being a bit inconsistent with caches?

Oke, raising error when use_cache=True but no Cache object is passed is a bad idea, that will break most of forward calls because people do not always set `cache=False` and `self.training` sometimes is not set to False. If we don't want to magically set default cache, we can raise warning and set `use_cache=False`. WDYT?

    inps = tokenizer("Hello, my dog is cute", return_tensors="pt")
    out = model(**inps, use_cache=True)
    print(f"{type(out) = }")
    print(f"{out.past_key_values = }")

### Expected behavior

I expect the `past_key_values` to be returned, as in `GemmaModel` and other `transformers` model families.

@kcarnold seems like Gemma2 doesn't work correctly with iterative forward, since it breaks a few things compared to the prev Gemma. I will make a PR soon to fix it, in the meanwhile you can make the above code work by preparing `cache_position` outside and passing it to forward as follows

It will output max diff of `3.8147e-05` between two logits

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers.cache_utils import HybridCache, DynamicCache

model_name = 'google/gemma-2-9b-it'
# model_name = 'google/gemma-1.1-2b-it'

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, device_map="cuda")

inps = tokenizer("1 3 2 4 5", return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
cache_position = torch.arange(inps.input_ids.shape[1], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
cache = HybridCache(config=model.config, max_batch_size=inps["input_ids"].shape[0], max_cache_len=20)
# cache = DynamicCache()

with torch.no_grad():
    out = model(inps.input_ids, cache_position=cache_position, use_cache=True, past_key_values=cache)

next_token = out.logits[0, -1].argmax()
cache_position_next = cache_position[-1:] + 1
print(next_token, repr(tokenizer.decode(next_token.item())))

concatted = torch.cat([inps["input_ids"], next_token.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)], dim=-1)
cache_position_concatted = torch.cat([cache_position, cache_position_next], dim=-1)

with torch.no_grad():
    out2_manual = model(concatted, cache_position=cache_position_concatted)
    out2_opt = model(next_token.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0), cache_position=cache_position_next, use_cache=True, past_key_values=cache)

    print((out2_manual.logits[0, -1] - out2_opt.logits[0, -1]).abs().max())
```

It is intentional: torch.compile does not support tensor updates in the graph.
